_comment: Vessel names that the automatic voyage-stripping rule cannot resolve on its own.
The rule in push-inbound-snapshot.mjs handles the ordinary cases: a trailing (...) group, a
trailing '/ ...' segment, and a trailing voyage CODE - digits with an E or W on one end, like
102E, E056, 6133W. That pattern is deliberately narrow so it cannot eat a ship's own number:
'WAN HAI A01' and 'WAN HAI 523' are left exactly as they are, because A01 and 523 match none
This file is for what the rule gets wrong or cannot know - the same curated-override habit as
ocean-routing's port_overrides.json. Keys are the RAW export string, lowercased and
whitespace-collapsed; values are the vessel name to group on.
Every push prints each distinct raw name beside what it became, so a new voyage spelling shows
up on the run that introduces it rather than as a duplicated ship on the map weeks later.
Empty today: the rule resolved every name in the 2026-09-03 export correctly, verified against
the three ONE HANNOVER spellings that were one sailing and the four WAN HAI A0x that are not.
